input.quote: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights or obligations hereunder, whether by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent, except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required.
input.rationale: Section 14.1 is mutual and contains an M&A/asset-sale carve-out, and there is no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right anywhere in the Agreement (Section 11 termination triggers are limited to uncured material breach and insolvency), so it is not in walk-away territory. However, it fails the fallback on a material term: consent for all other assignments (including to a Corio affiliate) is at the other party's absolute discretion, with no "not to be unreasonably withheld" standard, and Corio has no affiliate carve-out. Our redline adds the reasonableness qualifier and an affiliate carve-out for Corio while leaving the negotiated mutual merger carve-out and competitor exception intact, since the symmetric bargain makes the fully asymmetric preferred position disproportionate here.

proposal.summary: Qualify assignment consent as not unreasonably withheld and add an affiliate carve-out for Corio
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have qualified the consent standard so that consent to an assignment may not be unreasonably withheld, and added a carve-out allowing Corio to assign to its affiliates without consent. Our playbook does not accept an absolute consent right over customer assignments; the mutual merger/acquisition carve-out and the competitor exception are otherwise unchanged.
